description: Counts of participant-day transactions containing each one of the prespecified categorical items.
interpretation: Items occur at different frequencies; counts define the marginal support used by Apriori.
limitation: These are recorded categories in a small historical sample, not behavioral or health labels.
parameters: Prespecified step/activity bins; calories split at full-cohort Q1/Q3; weekday/weekend; Phase 2 completeness
subtitle: n=457 participant-days; participants=35; one item per family per day; zero-step records retained
title: Participant-day transaction item prevalence

description: Each point is a directed rule generated from a frequent itemset; green points satisfy every declared rule threshold.
interpretation: Eligibility additionally requires lift and distinct-participant support; a high confidence alone is insufficient.
legend: Eligible / not eligible under all prespecified thresholds
limitation: Rules are descriptive co-occurrences, not causal statements; repeated days from one person are not independent.
parameters: Apriori maximum itemset size 3; support 5%; confidence 60%; lift 1.10; minimum 5 distinct participants
subtitle: n=457 participant-days; 860 rules from itemsets of size 2-3; min support 5%, confidence 60%, lift 1.10, at least 5 participants
title: Association-rule support and confidence

description: Grouped bars compare the count of rules meeting all thresholds for the full cohort and complete-day subset.
interpretation: This prespecified grid shows how rule counts respond to support threshold changes and complete-day filtering.
limitation: Changing the threshold changes the candidate set; counts are not a measure of truth or predictive value.
subtitle: All-days n=457; complete-day n=233; confidence 60%, lift 1.10, minimum 5 participants
title: Eligible association rules across fixed support thresholds

description: Counts of low- and high-tail participant-day values beyond the linear-interpolated 1.5 times interquartile-range fences.
interpretation: The screen identifies distribution-tail records for review; different fields flag different rows.
legend: Below lower fence  Above upper fence
limitation: IQR fences do not establish errors, unusual physiology, or invalid wearables.
subtitle: n=457 participant-days; participants=35; linear-interpolated quartiles; values retained
title: Global 1.5×IQR candidate flags by field

description: Unique participant-day counts from the existing Phase 3 screen, new Phase 5 screens, and distinct distance definitions.
interpretation: Counts vary by method; overlapping methods can flag the same record and must not be added together.
limitation: Candidate counts are screening output, not counts of confirmed data errors.
parameters: Within-person |score| > 3.5; kNN top 5% with k=5/10; global 1.5×IQR; existing P3 flags retained
subtitle: n=457 participant-days; counts are per method; P1 strict absolute and Phase 2 distance flags remain separate
title: Candidate participant-days by screening method

description: Median and 95th-percentile mean-neighbor distance scores for pooled and completeness-stratified participant-day cohorts.
interpretation: Within-cohort percentiles show the upper score tail under pooled and coverage-stratified comparisons.
limitation: Each cohort is standardized separately; scores across cohorts are not directly interchangeable.
parameters: Features: steps/hour, calories/hour, active share; population-SD standardization; k=5/10; top 5% by cohort
subtitle: Rates standardized within each cohort; top 5% candidates; n=457 overall participant-days; k=5 and 10
title: kNN score distribution summaries by coverage cohort

description: Unique participant-days with an extreme within-person daily steps or active-share modified robust score.
interpretation: Within-person comparisons identify values unusual relative to each participant's own observed records.
limitation: Short and uneven observation histories limit each person's reference distribution; a flag is not an error diagnosis.
parameters: Modified MAD score threshold 3.5; at least 5 observed days; IQR fallback when MAD is zero and IQR positive
subtitle: n=457 participant-days; minimum 5 days per participant; absolute robust score threshold 3.5
title: Within-person robust candidate counts

description: Primary full-period candidate counts are compared with a sensitivity that excludes the last observed date.
interpretation: The all-date screen remains primary; the comparison shows the effect of omitting only the observed boundary date.
legend: Primary, all dates  Excluding final date
limitation: Phase 3 flags are reused then filtered rather than rerun; all other displayed screens are recalculated for sensitivity.
parameters: Primary retains April 12, 2016; sensitivity excludes that date; IQR, within-person, kNN and distance screens recalculated
subtitle: Primary n=457; final date=2016-04-12; primary includes all records; selected screens are recomputed
title: Last-date sensitivity for anomaly candidate counts
